Around our yard

Quick answers

The questions we hear most from farmers, builders and electricians.

What do Class 2 and Class 3 mean on your pressure pipes?

The class tells you how much pressure the pipe is made for. On Agarwal pressure pipes, Class 2 is rated 4 kgf/cm² and Class 3 is rated 6 kgf/cm². Our price list also covers 10 and 15 kgf/cm² for the smaller sizes. A higher class has a thicker wall, and the rating is printed along every length.

Which sizes do you make?

Plumbing and pressure pipes are priced from 20 mm (½ inch) up to 200 mm (8 inch). Electrical conduit is listed in 19, 20 and 25 mm. The price list above shows every size.

Which size and class do I need for my farm or house?

It depends on your motor, how long the line is and how high the water has to go. Tell us those three things on WhatsApp and we will suggest a size and class.

What is the difference between a pressure pipe and a conduit pipe?

Pressure pipes carry water. Conduit pipes protect electrical wires inside walls and slabs, and are not used for water.

What are casing pipes and column pipes?

A casing pipe lines a borewell. A column pipe hangs inside it and carries the water up from the submersible pump.

Do you also supply fittings?

Yes. Elbows, tees, bends, junction boxes and cover plates are part of our range, so one order can cover both the pipe and what joins it.

Do the prices include GST?

No. GST and all other applicable taxes are extra. Prices can change before an order is confirmed, and the price on your order invoice is the one charged.

How do I get a price?

Tap the price you need in the price list above, or tell us the pipe type, size, class, how many you need and where it is needed. The form below writes the message for you, and you just press send on WhatsApp.
